Item stack sizes fall back to 64 for 1,129 blocks until the data-pack reload supplies item components.

Mob-effect registry completed from the native report and MobEffects bytecode: 40 contiguous ids, with the new breath_of_the_nautilus at 39 (MobEffectCategory.BENEFICIAL, colour 65518, no attribute modifiers). client/data/effects.json now has 40 entries and Items merges the native 26.3 metadata over the unchanged 1.20.6 ids, so HUD labels, colours, blending and the jar's mob_effect sprite resolve for id 39.

Biome fallback table regenerated from the 26.3 jar (tools/port-26.3/build-biomes.mjs): 67 biomes in native alphabetical registry order, including dappled_forest (id 8), pale_garden and sulfur_caves; climate, precipitation and visual colours come from the jar data and display names from en_us.json. biomes:26.3 --check is part of test:26.3.

Enchantment table regenerated from the jar (tools/port-26.3/build-enchantments.mjs): 43 native alphabetical registry ids (aqua_affinity 0, lunge 21, wind_burst 42), with levels, costs, slots, supported items, exclusivity, membership tags and effects. enchantments:26.3 --check is part of test:26.3.

Food table regenerated from the native item-component reports (tools/port-26.3/build-foods.mjs): 44 foods with native item ids, nutrition and saturation, including the four 26.3 edible fish buckets and excluding the ominous bottle. foods:26.3 --check is part of test:26.3.

tasks.title: Binary primitives, text and component codecs
tasks.acceptance: Byte fixtures round-trip against native codecs, including the 26.3 component and dialog/waypoint families; complete packet consumption is asserted.
evidence: Native frames captured on 2026-11-25 from a disposable 26.3 server into tools/port-26.3/fixtures/login-config-26.3.json (30 frames, payload hex including the packet id).

byte-fixtures.mjs decodes them with the client's own Reader: compression threshold 256, Login Success uuid/name/properties, brand 'minecraft:brand'='vanilla', Update Enabled Features ['minecraft:vanilla'], Select Known Packs [minecraft:core:26.3]; every packet must be fully consumed.
Login Success re-encodes through the client's Writer to the exact native bytes.

Native change found by javap, not guessed: 26.3 renames the class to ClientboundLoginFinishedPacket and its STREAM_CODEC is composite(GAME_PROFILE, UUIDUtil.STREAM_CODEC), so Login Success carries a session UUID after the profile. The fixture asserts it (085cf48d-...).

Play codecs now cover Play Login, level_chunk_with_light, LpVec3 movement (add_entity, set_entity_motion), VecDelta movement (move_entity_pos/rot), PositionPath (entity_position_sync), light_update and the shared common packets.

Configuration codecs decode registry_data (Identifier + Optional anonymous NBT), update_tags (VarInt id lists), store_cookie, transfer, resource packs, code_of_conduct, show_dialog (inline anonymous NBT or registry id-1) and server_links (either a known link-type id or a component, then URL). Open: component serialization is read-only and the dialog screen is not presented yet.

tasks.title: Item components and stacks
tasks.acceptance: All 122 component types have a codec; patches and removals are preserved; defaults come from the native component reports.
evidence: Native codec manifest: component-codecs:26.3 runs javap on DataComponents and pins the networkSynchronized expression of all 122 registered component types; 7 are server-only (custom_data, intangible_projectile, map_decorations, debug_stick_state, recipes, lock, container_loot) and cannot appear in a patch.

ItemStack, ItemStackTemplate and DataComponentPatch decode from the javap layouts: VarInt count, VarInt item id, VarInt added/removed counts, values then removed ids. All 115 wire components have verified readers. can_place_on/can_break use AdventureModePredicate.STREAM_CODEC (javap): list of BlockPredicate{optional holderSet<Block>, optional StatePropertiesPredicate (exact/ranged either), optional NbtPredicate CompoundTag, DataComponentMatchers}. DataComponentMatchers is exact TypedDataComponent list plus list(64) of Type.STREAM_CODEC (either predicate-type or component-type id) followed by TypeBase's fromCodecWithRegistries anonymous CompoundTag. A byte-built gate covers direct holder sets, state property matchers, NBT, exact components and an explicit partial predicate.

Thirty previously fail-closed component readers joined: use_effects, attribute_modifiers (attribute holder, Identifier/double/operation modifier, slot group, default|hidden|override display), food, consumable (ItemUseAnimation, sound holder, five ConsumeEffect types), use_remainder, use_cooldown, damage_resistant, tool, weapon, attack_range, enchantable, equippable, repairable, tooltip_style, death_protection, blocks_attacks, piercing_weapon, kinetic_weapon, attack_animation, interact_animation, block_transformer, villager_food, profile (full GameProfile or partial plus PlayerSkin.Patch), compostable, cooking_fuel, brewing_fuel, mob_visibility, sign_text_front/back and cushion/color. DumpComponents26_3 binds the native item components, harvests a real value per item component and encodes it with Mojang's own stream codec; components:26.3 requires each reader to consume exactly those bytes (61 codecs checked, 29 of the 30 new readers oracle-verified; block_transformer is a dynamic-registry holder proven by javap).

Live 26.3 server, zero decode errors: a diamond_sword with damage=10 and a custom name, a diamond_pickaxe with enchantments [{enchantment:33,level:3}], two potions with potion_contents potion 13, a chest whose container component lists apple x5 and diamond x2, and a bundle with [apple x3, stick x8] all landed in the player inventory with the native component values.

window_items, set_slot and the 26.3-only set_player_inventory packet (aliased onto the existing windowId -2 path), close_window and craft_progress_bar are decoded and adapted; the pinned native window_items frame is consumed exactly by adapter:26.3.

Native enchantment holder ids resolve through client/js/net/enchantment-names-26.3.js, and the 43-entry table replaces the stale 766 order; Items keeps numeric 766 ids on the legacy mapping while resource-name ids use the native table. Gate coverage asserts the resolved names.

Native default components are generated from the 1658 native item reports by item-defaults:26.3 (client/js/net/item-defaults-26.3.js, 40 attributes ordered by protocol id) and checked in test:26.3. itemComponentValues26_3 merges the decoded patch over those defaults, deletes removed component ids and converts report/network shape differences (text NBT to components, attribute holder ids to names, rarity id to name, dyed colour, custom model data, potion holder id); Items.components selects it for every version 26.3 stack. The item-codec gate asserts diamond_sword max_damage 1561 with patched stack size 16/damage 42, removed unbreakable, apple food 4 and the scalar conversions. Adapted inventory slots carry the same version/defaults/removals (asserted on the native window frame), and the item view resolves an adapted slot's componentPatch additions and removals as well as raw stacks', so re-reading a slot never loses its patch. Native consumable animation ids map to names and drive useAction/useDuration: potion -> drink/32 ticks, apple -> eat/32 ticks. block-tags:26.3 resolves the jar's 300 block tag files into the 16 tag families used by native tool rules (nested tags expanded), and Items.strVsBlock applies the first matching tool rule: diamond pickaxe stone 8, sword cobweb 15/leaves 1.5, wooden axe stone 1. Native tooltip_display converts hidden component ids to names and suppresses the whole tooltip or the selected sections (enchantments, attributes, lore, dye, unbreakable and content-specific lines); the item gate covers hidden attributes and a fully hidden tooltip. Native equippable slot ids map to names and drive armorType (head/chest/legs/feet); body and saddle equipment stay out of player armor slots. Non-tool native items no longer consult the shifted 766 speed table. block-tools:26.3 runs a Java oracle over the native block registry to dump the 470 blocks whose default state requires the correct tool; with the native tool rules, canHarvest rejects wooden-on-iron-ore and hand-on-stone while accepting wooden-on-stone and diamond-on-obsidian. Nested ItemStackTemplates in bundle_contents, container, charged_projectiles, use_remainder and pot_decorations are adapted to decorated stack views, so bundle fullness and crossbow projectile tooltips read native contents. The gate covers a native bundle with two entries.

tasks.title: Login and Configuration lifecycle at protocol 777
evidence: The client's own socket (client/js/net/tcp-26.3.js + configuration-26.3.js) joins a disposable native 26.3 server on 2026-11-25: Hello/Login Finished, Login Acknowledged, Configuration (brand, update_enabled_features, select_known_packs, 30+ registry_data frames with anonymous-NBT payloads, update_tags, finish_configuration) and Play Login.

client-net.mjs drives VanillaSocket26_3 over Node TCP against 127.0.0.1:25568 and asserts the profile UUID, the 26.3 session UUID, 30+ registries with no elided payloads, 100+ tags, Play Login fields and byte-exact consumption of every decoded frame; login-config-frames.mjs replays 30 committed native frames through the same codecs, 23 of them registry_data.

Native behaviour proven, not assumed: claiming minecraft:core/26.3 without owning the pack makes the server omit every registry payload, so the client claims no packs and receives full data. A bad frame is still rejected with 'Badly compressed packet - size of 3 is below server threshold of 256'.
Open: the browser build still selects 766 through PROTOCOL_VERSION until the Play layer and client data are rebuilt.
tasks.acceptance: A disposable native 26.3 server accepts the offline join and completes Configuration with no mixed-version identity.

tasks.title: Complete essential Play path
tasks.acceptance: Every one of the 144 inbound Play IDs has a body and handler, and each of the 69 outbound IDs has a real sender or a recorded scope decision.
evidence: Play Login (id 50) decoded from the native fixture with zero trailing bytes on 2026-11-25: playerId 62, hardcore false, levels [overworld, the_end, the_nether], maxPlayers 5, chunkRadius 3, simulationDistance 3, showDeathScreen true, spawn dimension minecraft:overworld, seed 3819442548323920269, gamemode 0, isFlat false, portalCooldown 0, seaLevel 63, onlineMode false, enforcesSecureChat false.
Field order taken from javap on the native ClientboundLoginPacket, not from an older protocol schema; the seaLevel field is 26.3-era and is asserted.

Nine of the twelve captured Play frames now decode with exact consumption: change_difficulty, player_abilities, set_held_slot, entity_event, server_data, player_info_update, player_position, recipe_book_settings, commands. Still raw: update_recipes, recipe_book_add and the separately decoded login.

26.3 redesign found in the commands packet: argument types are a registry id into minecraft:command_argument_type (0-61, read from the native registries report) followed by ArgumentTypeInfo.deserializeFromNetwork properties, not the 1.20.6 parser name string. A new restricted flag (bit 32) exists. The captured 26-node tree decodes to zero leftover and resolves int_range, message, string, entity, objective and integer parsers.
26.3 network NBT confirmed from NbtIo.writeAnyTag bytecode: tag id only, no root name. Reading server_data with the named-root reader underflowed; the anonymous reader consumes it exactly.
Player info update actions are a fixed 1-byte bitset over the eight actions (FriendlyByteBuf.writeFixedBitSet), not a VarInt mask.

Chunk path landed: level_chunk_with_light decodes all 9 captured native chunks with zero leftover (24 sections, heightmaps, block entities, light byte-array layers). Validated against the jar's own registry: every section nonEmptyBlockCount equals the number of non-air states unpacked, and all state ids are below the native 35,723.

26.3 chunk findings from bytecode: a section now carries two shorts (nonEmptyBlockCount, fluidCount); BitStorage packs floor(64/bits) values per long, so 5-bit sections are 342 longs and not 320; biome containers hold 64 entries; BIT_SET is a byte array, not a long array. Name mapping shows 26.2 cinnabar and sulfur in the caves at y=0.

Live-world layer added: set_time (26.3 clock map), game_event, chunk batch start/finished, chunk cache center, spawn position, health, experience, border (now includes warningTime), block_update, section_blocks_update (VarLong state<<12|pos). Forty-three of 51 captured startup frames decode with zero leftover and a live join decodes 100+ Play frames across 30+ types; 46 inbound IDs have javap-verified decoders.

Native redesigns recorded from the jar: LpVec3 (48-bit packed vector), VecDelta packed as (stepCount<<1)|onGround with Linear/Stepped steps, PositionPath stepped paths carrying only steps, 26.3 serverbound accept_teleportation echoing position and rotation, and horizontalCollision on move packets.

Join context is built from native configuration data (session-26.3.js): 35,723 block states and the air set from the block report, biome holder ids, dimension types decoded from registry NBT with 26.3's Skybox/attributes replacing effects, feature flags and tag registries. client-net.mjs asserts the overworld type is min_y -64 / height 384 / skylight.

Open: 46 of 144 inbound Play IDs decoded; entity metadata/equipment, item-stack components, advancements and the redesigned recipes remain raw. No Play handlers, no chunk/entity/registry consumers, and entity_position_sync's stepped path was proven by a 39-byte native frame.

Play adapter (play-adapter-26.3.js) maps decoded 26.3 packets onto real on_<handler> names from game.js; adapter:26.3 replays 53 pinned native frames and asserts 22 packets across 16 handlers, including two 24-section chunks loaded through world.loadChunk26_3 and native light masks.

Live 26.3 server session: the native server accepted the client after the serverbound bodies were corrected from bytecode - accept_teleportation now echoes position and rotation, movement packets carry the packed onGround/horizontalCollision flags byte, every client tick ends with client_tick_end (which clears the server's per-tick position flag), and keep_alive/ping are adapted back to the game handlers. The session stayed connected past the keepalive timeout with no invalid-packet disconnect.

Entity Play path landed on 2026-11-26: add_entity resolves the native minecraft:entity_type registry (161 dense ids) to names, set_entity_data decodes the native EntityDataSerializers table (44 ids dumped from getSerializedId after Bootstrap) and set_equipment reads the continuation-bit slot list. 49 of 144 inbound Play IDs now have bytecode-verified decoders; adapter:26.3 replays 53 pinned frames, adapting 29 packets across 18 handlers and asserting both native bats plus five metadata frames.

Particle metadata closed the last live join decode gap: entity metadata serializer 17 (PARTICLES) decodes all 128 registered particle types through their native StreamCodecs, so a fresh 26.3 join loads 81 chunks and 26 entities with zero skipped frames (the same join previously skipped 56 frames, all [set_entity_data#101] serializer 17).
Outbound click and attack are live-accepted: container_click round-trips the menu state id (1 -> 2) and moves a stack, and the native attack body removes a summoned pig after 8 hits.

Inbound batch on 2026-11-26: 73 of 144 Play IDs now decode with bytecode-verified bodies and 51 have adapters. Added animate, take_item_entity, hurt_animation, block_event, level_event, player_rotation, set_title_text/subtitle/action bar, set_titles_animation, clear_titles, system_chat, disguised_chat, tab_list, set_passengers, set_entity_link, player_info_remove, set_cursor_item and teleport_entity; inbound-gate.mjs pins each byte layout and the adapted handler fields.

Live 26.3 checks: server /say arrived as disguised_chat and rendered in chat, /title rendered the gold component in the HUD, an item summoned at the player was collected through take_item_entity (stone 8 -> 9), and the session stayed at zero skipped frames.

Vehicle movement (PositionAndRotation), block-change acknowledgements and remote block destruction joined the inbound set (76 of 144 decode). Live /gamemode survival arrived as game_event id 3 and switched the client from creative to survival with zero skipped frames.

Distance, camera, pong and combat-event frames followed (82 of 144 decode, 60 adapters). The local 26.3 server reports view-distance=3 and simulation-distance=3, and a fresh join now sets both client values from the decoded packets with zero skipped frames.

Boss-event frames joined the inbound set (83 of 144 decode, 61 adapters): all six operations read the native UUID + VarInt action layout, with anonymous-NBT name, f32 progress, colour/overlay VarInts and the flags byte. Live 26.3 check: /bossbar add plus /bossbar set ... players delivered operation 0 and hud.bossBars held BOSS5 with progress, colour, overlay and flags; the update operations are byte-gated only, not yet exercised live.

Sound, cooldown and mob-effect frames joined the inbound set (89 of 144 decode, 67 adapters). Bytecode established that sound and effect registries travel as holders with wire id = protocol id + 1 (0 = inline value), that sound events also carry a 26.3 UI source (11 categories), and that effect flags are ambient/visible/icon/blend. The native sound-event and mob-effect name tables are generated and checked by generate-ids; the adapter maps effects onto the 1.20.6 ids the HUD uses and cooldowns through the native item table. Verified by byte fixtures and by client-net:26.3 decoding a real 33-chunk session against the local 26.3 server; browser quest for live /playsound, /effect and /stopsound was started but the page did not reach Play in this low-disk environment.

Chunk unload, block-entity data, sign editor and advancement-tab selection followed (93 of 144 decode, 71 adapters). ChunkPos is one packed long (x low 32 bits, z high 32 bits) after javap showed readChunkPos/writeChunkPos delegating to pack/unpack; block-entity data carries the registry type id and an anonymous compound tag, and SignTextSlot is BACK=0/FRONT=1. All four are byte-gated and the real-server client-net run decodes 29 chunks with zero leftover frames.

Respawn, player-look-at, open-book and command-suggestions frames followed (97 of 144 decode, 75 adapters). CommonPlayerSpawnInfo's GameType is a VarInt with an OPTIONAL_VAR_INT previous type (0 = none), verified from GameType's own codec, and respawn reuses the 766 spawn-info vocabulary so the existing dimension resolver and death screen apply; suggestions carry VarInt id/start/length plus text and optional component tooltips. Byte-gated and the full test, adapter and real-server client-net suites stayed green.

Custom chat completions, tag-query responses and display-objective frames followed (100 of 144 decode, 78 adapters). The completion Action enum is ADD/REMOVE/SET in native order, tag queries carry transaction id + network NBT for the inspect path, and DisplaySlot is the VarInt the scoreboard handler already consumes. Gate, test, adapter and real-server client-net all stayed green.

Container windows, chat deletion and custom payloads joined the adapted set (102 of 144 decode, 80 adapters). open_screen needed no renumbering table: the 26.3 menu registry report has the same 25 identifiers in the same order as protocol 766, so the native registry id is also the menuInfo766 id and on_open_window resolves slot counts unchanged. delete_chat follows MessageSignature.Packed (VarInt id+1, 0 means a full 256-byte signature) and the adapter shifts the 0-based packed id onto the 1-based MessageSignatureCache762. custom_payload was already decoded as channel + rest bytes but had no adapter, so minecraft:brand never reached on_custom_payload; it now does. All three are byte-gated, including a full 256-byte signature and both brand and opaque payloads.

Adapter audit closed the decoded-but-unwired gameplay set (102 decode, 91 adapters): commands, player_info_update, server_data, change_difficulty, entity_event, section_blocks_update, level_particles, ticking_state, ticking_step, set_chunk_cache_center and initialize_border now reach on_declare_commands, on_player_info, on_server_data, on_difficulty, on_entity_status, on_multi_block_change, on_world_particles, on_set_ticking_state, on_step_tick, on_update_view_position and on_initialize_world_border. section_blocks_update unpacks SectionPos x(22)/z(22)/y(20) and the section-relative short layout x(8)/z(4)/y(0); initialize_border maps initialise sizes onto WorldBorder's action-3 vocabulary. Only six socket/lifecycle packets plus player_rotation, recipe_book_settings, bundle_delimiter and post_effects remain unwired from the decoded set. Gate and real-server client-net stayed green (27 chunks).

The death-screen path joined (103 decode, 92 adapters): player_combat_kill is playerId VarInt + trusted NBT message, adapted onto a new on_death_combat_event that reuses the existing combat-event death branch. Byte-gated with a string message.

Scoreboard and teams joined (107 decode, 96 adapters): set_score, set_objective, reset_score and set_player_team decode the native optional NumberFormat dispatch (blank/fixed supported; styled stays fail-closed) and the team Parameters order (three components, visibility/collision enums, optional TeamColor, friendly-fire byte). reset_score and teams get thin Game handlers so the generated handled map includes them; the scoreboard vocabulary is unchanged. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

World border family closed (116 decode, 105 adapters): initialize plus the five setters now decode native fields and feed the existing 0-5 world-border vocabulary, with diameters halved exactly as the 766 handler expects. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

Player chat joined (111 decode, 100 adapters): the native packet reads the optional 256-byte signature, packed body with last-seen signature ids, optional unsigned component, filter mask (byte-array bitset only when partially filtered) and bound chat type (holder id, name, optional target). The adapter feeds the existing chat handler. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

Maps and swing animation joined (110 decode, 99 adapters): map_item_data reads the optional decoration list and optional MapPatch, flattening both into the existing item-map update shape; swing_animation reads the VarInt entity id and byte action through an on_swing_animation bridge. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

Biome updates joined (108 decode, 97 adapters): chunks_biomes reads the native list of packed ChunkPos longs plus VarInt-prefixed section buffers and hands the existing palette path the exact byte payload. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

Server links and clear-dialog joined (130 decode, 109 adapters): each ServerLinks entry is a boolean-tagged Either (true = KnownLinkType idMapper id, false = trusted context-free component) followed by the URL string; clear_dialog is a unit codec. A live Chrome join on the local 26.3 server rendered terrain, health/hunger and the hotbar with no decode error, and the advancement/statistics screens stay honestly empty until their raw packets are ported. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

The recipe family joined (134 decode, 109 adapters): update_recipes is a VarInt map of RecipePropertySet Identifiers to item-id lists plus the stonecutter SingleInputSet; recipe_book_add is a list of RecipeDisplayEntry (VarInt display id, RecipeDisplay registry-dispatch payload, optional group, RecipeBookCategory id, optional Ingredient holder-set list) with a flags byte and replace boolean; recipe_book_remove is a list of VarInt display ids; place_ghost_recipe is a container id and a RecipeDisplay. The SLOT_DISPLAY and RECIPE_DISPLAY orders come from the 26.3 generated report, and the live burst's update_recipes and recipe_book_add frames consume exactly with zero leftover.

Tags, game rules, report details, disk warning, transient blocks, mount screens, debug samples and test frames joined (128 decode, 109 adapters): update_tags maps a registry Identifier to a tag payload of tag Identifiers and VarInt entry ids and is flattened onto the 766 tag list; game_rule_values is an Identifier/string map; custom_report_details is a string/string map; low_disk_space_warning is a unit codec; add_transient_block is a BlockPos plus block-state id; mount_screen_open is writeContainerId, VarInt columns and a full writeInt entityId; debug_sample is a long array plus the sample-type ordinal and feeds the existing tick-time handler; game_test_highlight_pos is two BlockPos values; test_instance_block_status is a component plus an optional Vec3i. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

Damage events and projectile power joined (119 decode, 107 adapters): damage_event is VarInt entityId plus a DamageType holder, the cause/direct ids as id+1 (0 absent) and an optional Vec3; the adapter undoes the +1 for the existing handler. projectile_power is now a VarInt id and a single double accelerationPower, so it stays decoded without an adapter instead of inventing a Vec3 direction for the 766 fireball path. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

Merchant offers joined (117 decode, 106 adapters): ClientboundMerchantOffersPacket is the container id (writeContainerId), the MerchantOffers list, then VarInt villagerLevel, VarInt villagerXp and the showProgress/canRestock booleans; MerchantOffer.writeToStream is ItemCost, ItemStack, optional ItemCost, isOutOfStock, then uses/maxUses/xp/specialPriceDiff as writeInt (a 26.3 change from 766 VarInts), float priceMultiplier and writeInt demand. ItemCost is a VarInt item holder, VarInt count and a DataComponentExactPredicate list of TypedDataComponent pairs; the adapter feeds the existing trade_list screen shape. Gate, test and real-server client-net stayed green.

Advancements joined (135 decode, 110 adapters): ClientboundUpdateAdvancementsPacket is the reset flag, a list of PositionedAdvancement (Identifier, Advancement, float x/y), a removed Identifier set, an Identifier -> AdvancementProgress map and the show flag. Advancement.STREAM_CODEC sends only optional parent, optional DisplayInfo, AdvancementRequirements and the telemetry flag (no rewards or criteria map); DisplayInfo writes title/description components, an ItemStackTemplate icon, the AdvancementType ordinal and one flags int (background/toast/hidden) with the background Identifier when bit 0 is set; each criterion progress is an optional epoch-millis instant. DumpAdvancements26_3 encodes the packet with Mojang's own StreamCodec and the gate decodes those 224 bytes field for field, then the adapter feeds the existing advancement manager. The live-burst adapter count rose from 41 to 42 packets and 29 to 30 handlers. Gate and test stayed green.

Explosions joined (136 decode, 111 adapters): ClientboundExplodePacket is a Vec3 centre, float radius, int blockCount, an optional Vec3 knockback, the explosion ParticleOptions, a sound holder, a WeightedList<ExplosionParticleInfo> (value then VarInt weight) and a playSound flag; 26.3 no longer sends destroyed-block offsets. The gate decodes 82 bytes encoded by Mojang's own StreamCodec. Client behaviour changed with it: Game.on_explosion plays the packet sound only when playSound is set, spawns one explosion particle with velocity (1,0,0), applies the optional knockback and feeds ClientExplosionTracker, ported to client/js/game/explosion-tracker.js (512-particle cap, weighted picks, particle-setting clearing, solid-block rejection) and ticked with the client tick. Gate, test and the existing 1.20.6-shaped explosion playback test stayed green.

Statistics and minecart steps joined (138 decode, 112 adapters). award_stats is a VarInt map whose key is Stat.STREAM_CODEC: the STAT_TYPE registry id followed by the id in that type's value registry; DumpStats26_3 encodes 13 bytes with Mojang's codec and also dumps the native stat_type and custom_stat orders. The 26.3 custom registry inserts happy_ghast_one_cm (17), nautilus_one_cm (22) and sleep_in_straw_bed (61), so StatsCounter now accepts native type/custom tables and the statistics screen uses them instead of the shifted 1.20.6 list. move_minecart_along_track decodes a VarInt entity id and MinecartStep entries (position Vec3, movement Vec3, two rotation bytes, float weight); it has no 766 handler, so it is decoded-only rather than given an invented adapter. Gate and test stayed green.

Tracked waypoint joined the client surface on 2026-11-27: the native packet body (operation, Either<UUID,String>, icon style + optional RGB, four payload shapes) is decoded and adapted, ClientWaypointManager track/update/untrack is ported, and the native locator bar draws the 60-degree window, distance sprites and pitch arrows. A browser-injected tracked waypoint rendered the bar; a real server /waypoint command was not exercised.

Respawn was fixed against a live death on the 26.3 server: the packet carries a dimension-type holder id, so the adapter now resolves it through the join context registry. The client returned to the overworld with 20 health and no respawn exception; the previous build threw Missing or invalid 762 dimension 0.

show_dialog joined the decoded set on 2026-11-27 (140 of 144, 113 adapters, 4 raw): Dialog.STREAM_CODEC is ByteBufCodecs.holder(Registries.DIALOG, fromCodecWithRegistriesTrusted(DIRECT_CODEC)), so the body is VarInt 0 plus one unnamed NBT tag for a direct dialog, otherwise registry id-1. The gate covers both branches. Presenting the dialog graph as a screen remains open because DialogScreen needs the body/input/action handlers, which are not ported yet.

evidence: Connection opens VanillaSocket26_3 for protocol 777, builds the join context on play_login and adapts every Play packet before the game sees it. The browser build still selects 766 until the 26.3 model/shape data lands.

Native graphical join in Chrome on 2026-11-26: the 26.3 client built its join context from the native registry report, spawned at (4.4747, 70.0, 5.1511), streamed and rendered 81 chunks with terrain, tall grass and sky, and showed the full HUD (10 hearts, hunger bar, hotbar). The server logged the join with no movement or keepalive disconnect, and the client reported inWorld=true, doneLoadingTerrain=true and crashed=false.

P07 acceptance is complete: terrain, entities, HUD, movement, death/respawn and reconnect were all exercised live. The browser now serves 26.3 block models, textures and the 26.3 panorama; entity rigs 26.3 restructured still use the 1.20.6 part trees (P10).

Live 26.3 entity rendering verified in Chrome on 2026-11-26: the client tracked 83 entities with sane coordinates (max |x|/|z| = 56), including pigs, sheep, cows, chickens, bats, villagers, glow squid and the 26.3 sulfur_cube (raw identity, no 1.20.6 model). Cow, sheep, pig and chicken models rendered in-world; health and bat flags decoded from native set_entity_data frames.

Movement verified against the 26.3 server: holding forward for 1.6 s moved the player 6.9 blocks (+Z 1.56 -> 8.46) and the server accepted every move packet. The embedded preview webview cannot grant pointer lock (WrongDocumentError), so input state was driven directly instead of through a locked mouse.

Death/respawn and reconnect verified: a summoned zombie killed the player (server logged "was slain by Zombie"), the DeathScreen respawn round-tripped client_command and restored health 20 in creative, and repeated disconnect/reconnect joins all reached Play.
